what: Case study - 2013/14 DENV3 outbreak in Fiji
title: Estimate relative R0 from temperature data for vector-borne diseases with {climateR0}
text: first case study, ’ll use data 2013/4 DENV-3 outbreak Fiji. show laboratory confirmed cases time Central Division.  dataset, time-series monthly mean temperatures (°C) Central Division, Fiji. extract corresponding temperature-dependent R0 values temperature-relative R0 curves estimated Mordecai et al, use temperature_R0() function. Within function call, specify vector-pathogen code AeaeDENV vector Aedes aegypti pathogen dengue virus. Now can plot relative temperature-dependent R0 values alongside case data.   discussed Kucharski et al (2018), comparing case time series temperature-dependent R0 indicates fall transmission due seasonal temperature variation fully explain fall cases March 2014. paper, Kucharski colleagues found model including build-herd immunity decrease transmission resulting vector control campaign March 2024 better captured observed pattern cases.
code: fiji_cases <- fiji_2014 |>   ggplot() +   geom_line(aes(x = date, y = cases), col = "#016c59") +   scale_x_date(breaks = "month", date_labels = "%b-%y") +   labs(x = "Date", y = "Reported dengue cases") +   theme_classic()  fiji_cases fiji_2014$rR0 <- temperature_r0(fiji_2014$av_temp, "AeaeDENV") #> Returning relative R0 for vector: aedes_aegypti and pathogen: dengue_virus fiji_rR0 <- fiji_2014 |>   ggplot() +   geom_line(aes(x = date, y = rR0), col = "#54278f") +   scale_x_date(breaks = "month", date_labels = "%b-%y") +   labs(x = "Date", y = "Relative R0") +   theme_classic()  fiji_rR0 plot_grid(fiji_cases, fiji_rR0, nrow = 2)

title: Estimate relative R0 from temperature data for vector-borne diseases with {climateR0}
text: models used account aspects weather climate variability likely influence vector-borne disease dynamics, including variation precipitation, relative humidity, temperature time. approach also account time lags temperature R0; instead, calculates static snapshot relative temperature suitability transmission given point time, assuming temperature constant point. reality, multiple time lags may relevant R0. example, temperature 4-8 weeks ago may affect mosquito population size development rate, whereas temperature 2-4 weeks ago may affect vector competence extrinsic incubation period. Despite limitations, temperature-dependent relative R0 used predict geographical temporal variation different settings malaria, dengue, Zika, Ross River virus West Nile virus (details references ). Mordecai et al 2017 Tesla et al 2018 Shocket et al 2018 Shocket et al 2020 Childs et al 2024

title: Simple short-term forecasting with relative R0
text: First, calculate temperature-dependent R0 values using mean temperature. next define function weight lagged cases dengue serial interval. Now wrangle Fiji 2014 data forecasting set forecast horizon (many weeks ahead want forecast) dates like forecasts start .
code: fiji_2014$rR0 <- temperature_r0(fiji_2014$av_temp, "AeaeDENV") # Function to weight past cases by dengue serial interval # From Siraj et al 2017  weight_cases <- function(x) {   lag(x, 2) * 0.2 + lag(x, 3) * 0.425 + lag(x, 4) * 0.25 + lag(x, 5) * 0.125 } pop <- 342000  model_data <- fiji_2014 |>   dplyr::mutate(date_numeric = as.numeric(date - min(date) + 1)) |>   dplyr::arrange(date) |>   dplyr::mutate(     cumulative_cases = cumsum(cases),     pop_susceptible = 1 - (cumulative_cases / pop),     weighted_lagged_cases = weight_cases(cases),     log_weighted_lagged_cases = log(weighted_lagged_cases + 0.001),     log_pop_susceptible = log(pop_susceptible + 0.001)   )  horizon <- 2 prediction_dates <- seq(   from = as.Date("2014-02-06"),   to = as.Date("2014-09-01"),   by = 7 )

title: Simple short-term forecasting with relative R0
text: now generate 2-week ahead forecasts prediction dates.
code: all_forecasts <- NULL weekly_forecasts <- NULL  for (prediction_start in prediction_dates){  prediction_start <- as.Date(prediction_start)  message(   "Generating forecasts for prediction week starting: ",   as.Date(prediction_start, origin = "1970-01-01") ) train_data <- model_data |>   dplyr::filter(date <= prediction_start)  # Run gam model  gam_mod <- mgcv::gam(   formula = cases ~ s(rR0, bs = "bs", k = 5, m = 2) +     s(log_weighted_lagged_cases, bs = "bs", k = 5, m = 2) +     offset(log_pop_susceptible),   family = "nb",   data = train_data)  # nolint start: line_length_linter  # Set up testing rows prediction_rows <- data.frame(   date = as.Date(prediction_start, origin = "1970-01-01") + seq(7, 7 * horizon, by = 7),   date_numeric = max(train_data$date_numeric) + seq(7, 7 * horizon, by = 7),   rR0 = rep(tail(train_data$rR0, 1), horizon),   log_pop_susceptible = rep(tail(train_data$log_pop_susceptible, 1), horizon),   log_weighted_lagged_cases = rep(tail(train_data$log_weighted_lagged_cases, 1), horizon),   cases = rep(NA, horizon) ) # nolint end  train_test_data <-   rbind(     train_data |> dplyr::select( # nolint: nested_pipe_linter       date, date_numeric, rR0, log_pop_susceptible,       log_weighted_lagged_cases, cases     ),     prediction_rows   )  # Generate samples from posterior estimates samples <- posterior_samples(   model = gam_mod,   data = train_test_data,   n = 1000,   method = "mh" ) |>   dplyr::rename(     .sample = .draw,     .value = .response   )  # Aggregate samples to quantiles prediction_out <- samples |>   dplyr::group_by(.row) |>   dplyr::summarise(     median = median(.value, na.rm = TRUE),     q_0.025 = quantile(.value, 0.0025, na.rm = TRUE),     q_0.975 = quantile(.value, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),     q_0.25 = quantile(.value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),     q_0.75 = quantile(.value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)   ) |>   dplyr::select(-.row) |>   dplyr::mutate(prediction_start = prediction_start)  prediction_out <- cbind(train_test_data |> select(date), prediction_out) |> # nolint: pipe_continuation_linter   dplyr::mutate(type = case_when(date > prediction_start ~ "forecast",                    T ~ "fit"))  # Plot for current forecast cols <- c(fit = "#8e0152", forecast = "#276419")  current_forecast <- prediction_out |>   cbind(train_test_data |> select(cases)) |> # nolint: pipe_continuation_linter   ggplot2::ggplot() +   ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(x = date, y = median, col = type)) +   ggplot2::geom_ribbon(     ggplot2::aes(       x = date,       ymin = q_0.025,       ymax = q_0.975,       fill = type     ),     alpha = 0.2   ) +   ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(x = date, y = cases)) +   ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +   ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = cols) +   ggplot2::scale_x_date(labels = scales::label_date_short()) +   ggplot2::labs(x = "Confirmed cases cases", y = "Date", fill = "", col = "") +   ggplot2::theme_bw()  weekly_forecasts[[match(prediction_start, prediction_dates)]] <- current_forecast # nolint: line_length_linter all_forecasts <- rbind(all_forecasts, prediction_out) }  formatted_forecasts <- merge(   all_forecasts |> filter(type == "forecast"),   model_data |> dplyr::select(cases, date),   by = "date",   all = TRUE ) |>   dplyr::mutate(     prediction_start = as.Date(prediction_start, origin = "1970-01-01")   )

text: plot 2-week ahead forecasts (different colours depending prediction start date), compare predictions observed dengue data (black). line shows median predicted value shaded area shows 95% prediction interval.  can also look forecasts specific weeks.
